findings.evidence: PRD R10 + AC-12 mandate that on every synthesis run the skill recomputes sprint-bucket from Depends-on + Scope and aborts with a diagnostic pointing the user to `specflow:scope-change` if the existing tasks file's values disagree. But `plugins/specflow/skills/scope-change/SKILL.md` Phase E ('Delta task regeneration') itself fans back through the task synthesis path — scope-change is the legitimate channel for edits to Depends-on. Between the moment scope-change rewrites a task's Depends-on edges and the moment it re-invokes synthesis on the delta, the existing `{NNN-slug}-tasks.md` on disk still carries the pre-edit sprint-bucket values. The recompute-and-compare check will trigger on those very tasks, abort, and instruct the user to run `specflow:scope-change` — which is what just ran. The PRD never specifies how the check distinguishes 'graph legitimately changed by scope-change, re-bucketing required' from 'user hand-edited the field' — they look identical to a recompute-vs-existing diff. The same false-positive applies to any in-place edit of Depends-on the skill itself performs during Phase D.4 self-correction or D revisions in Phase E rounds.
findings.claim: Architectural gotcha + cross-artefact drift — R10's enforcement check assumes the only source of (existing tasks-file value ≠ recomputed value) is a hand-edit. But the upstream task graph itself is mutable (via specflow:scope-change, and via this skill's own Phase E.4 round-2 edits per `task/SKILL.md` lines 380-381). The PRD's diagnostic and routing are circular for the legitimate scope-change path, and the check has no way to attribute the mismatch to the actual cause. This is a cross-artefact contract failure between 025 and the `scope-change` skill that the PRD's R10 trace ('this implies the field is derived, not authored') does not engage with.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) scope the recompute-and-compare check to only fire when the existing tasks-file's `Depends on:` edges and `Scope:` surfaces are byte-identical to what the current synthesis input encodes — i.e. only flag 'output diverged with inputs unchanged', the actual hand-edit signature; (b) gate the check behind a synthesis-mode flag that scope-change suppresses on its delta-regeneration call; or (c) drop R10/AC-12 entirely (per simplicity-reviewer's separate finding) and rely on the read-only contract being documentation-level. Whichever route, the PRD must explicitly reconcile with `scope-change`'s delta-regeneration path or it ships a circular diagnostic.

findings.evidence: PRD R6 trace: 'tuning the bucket count is a 022-cross-task-review concern.' Non-goals echo: 'Auto-detecting the optimal number of buckets … is a 022-cross-task-review concern.' But `v2/docs/FEATURES.md` § 022 (Sprint 2, target v2.6.0) defines 022's two lenses as (1) coherence — do tasks work together, all trace to PRD requirements + goal, and (2) better arrangement — could two tasks merge, could one split, is there a different ordering. § 029 § Implications #2 echoes 022's 'better arrangement lens explicitly checks: are any tasks oversized? Should two tasks merge to share context? Should one split because its budget overflows?' None of those framings include 'auto-tune the sprint-bucket count.' 022 hasn't shipped, so its scope can still absorb this — but the PRD is parking work in another feature's surface without that feature having explicitly opted in.
findings.claim: Cross-artefact drift / cross-feature dependency — 025 silently delegates 'auto-tuning bucket count' to 022, but 022's documented scope (per FEATURES.md and 029's Implications) is task-merge/task-split/re-ordering, not bucket-count tuning. If 022 lands as currently scoped, the auto-tuning concern has no home and will surface as a follow-up amendment. This is a downstream-coupling assumption the PRD's Open Questions section claims is 'all resolved' — but the resolution depends on a feature that hasn't been written.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) tighten the Non-goal/R6-trace prose to 'tuning the bucket count is out of scope here; whether it lands in 022 or a future feature is a separate planning decision' — i.e. don't claim 022 owns it; (b) add a one-line note to 022's brief in `v2/docs/FEATURES.md` capturing that 025 expects 022 to absorb bucket-count tuning, so the dependency is documented at both ends; or (c) demote it to a known open question rather than asserting the routing is resolved.

findings.evidence: PRD R7 + AC-13 specify the phase ordering as `task/SKILL.md` Phase D verify-steps: '(a) per-task budget check (029 R4); (b) bucket assignment (R2); (c) topological-floor invariant check (R9).' R2 also says 'Document the bucket-assignment heuristic in task/SKILL.md Phase D verify-steps.' But the existing `task/SKILL.md` has its budget check inside Phase B.4 ('Budget self-check (per 029-single-context-task)' on line 208), not in Phase D. Phase D in the existing skill is 'Override capture'; Phase E is 'Gate 3 multi-agent debate manifest.' There is no current 'Phase D verify-steps' section in the skill — the skill's verify-style steps live across B.4 (self-check) and the standalone 'Verify before declaring done' tail (line 460). The PRD repeatedly mandates code-anchored placement against a phase that doesn't house what the PRD claims it houses.
findings.claim: Cross-artefact drift / blast-radius underestimate — the PRD's prescriptive phase-naming ('Phase D verify-steps') does not match the existing skill's structure. Either the PRD intends to RE-shape Phase D (a non-trivial restructure not captured in any R), or it is using 'Phase D' as a casual label for 'the verify pass' (which currently lives in B.4 and the tail). Without resolution, the implementer faces a fork — restructure the skill or relocate the new content — neither of which the PRD's Goals or Requirements scope acknowledge. The skill-size ceiling (R8) and the 14-line headroom argument depend on no restructure happening; a Phase D rewrite breaks that headroom assumption.
findings.proposed_change: Replace every 'Phase D verify-steps' reference in R2/R7/R9/AC-2/AC-4/AC-12/AC-13 with the actual current home — either `Phase B.4 Self-check` (where the 029 budget check already sits) or a new explicitly-named subsection (e.g. `Phase B.4.1 Bucket assignment` and `Phase B.4.2 Topological-floor invariant`). If the PRD's intent IS to restructure into a real Phase D verify-steps section, surface that as its own R with its own line-budget impact (this materially changes R8's headroom maths).

findings.evidence: Users section lists four user types, the fourth being 'The sprint-skill (020) itself. Programmatic consumer.' The interview's Sign-off captured the field as a single-integer artefact written by `specflow:task`; consumer-side semantics are explicitly out-of-scope (Non-goals 1: 'Building the sprint-skill itself (020). 025 produces the field; 020 consumes it. The two are deliberately separated.'). Including 020 as a User in the same section as direct human users implicitly elevates it to a contract-shaping stakeholder — which is exactly what Non-goal 1 says it is not.
findings.claim: Cross-artefact drift — listing the as-yet-unbuilt sister feature as a User leaks 020's interface concerns back into 025's PRD scope. If 020's eventual implementation needs different field semantics (e.g. a `sprint-bucket-confidence` overlay, or feature-scoped vs cross-feature numbering), the Users-list framing makes 025 the contract owner who must change. The interview deliberately deferred those decisions; the PRD silently re-imports them.
findings.proposed_change: Move 020 out of the Users section. Either (a) drop the bullet entirely (the Goals already say '020 reads it without recomputing topology'); or (b) move it to a new 'Downstream consumers (informational)' note that explicitly disclaims contract authority — '025 writes the field per R1-R10; how 020 reads it is 020's concern.' The point of Non-goal 1 is preserved either way.

findings.evidence: R8 asserts `task/SKILL.md` is at 486 lines with ~14 lines of headroom. The PRD's additions, even with the most aggressive prose-tightening, include: R2's three-input heuristic with fixpoint definition + lexicographic disambiguation, R7's phase-ordering prose + AC-13's verbatim-listing requirement, R9's topological-floor invariant verify-step, R10's recompute-and-compare check + AC-12's diagnostic message specification (task ID, existing value, recomputed value, scope-change pointer), AC-3's worked-example fixture (three tasks demonstrating the parallelism overlay), and AC-11's hand-edit-affordance-absence audit. Realistic prose for that surface is 30+ lines, not 14. The Goals section lists 'Existing prose tightening is part of the work' under R8 but neither identifies which sections compress nor quantifies the savings.
findings.claim: Blast-radius underestimate — R8's 14-line headroom claim assumes the rest of the work fits in 14 lines, but the PRD itself enumerates additions (R2 heuristic + R7 ordering + R9 invariant + R10 enforcement + AC-3 worked example + AC-12 diagnostic) whose prose budget exceeds 14 lines under any reasonable density assumption. The PRD's resolution ('existing prose tightening') is asserted, not scoped. This is a stealth blast-radius — the implementer either breaks the ceiling or carves into existing sections in ways the PRD doesn't authorise.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) name the sections being tightened and the line-target per section, so R8's headroom claim is auditable; (b) raise the ceiling explicitly by amending R8 to a higher cap (e.g. 540) with the chain-don't-absorb feedback as the load-bearing argument that this is a justified exception; or (c) extract the heuristic + worked example into a sibling doc (e.g. `templates/task/sprint-bucket-heuristic.md`) and have `task/SKILL.md` cite it, mirroring how 029 uses `templates/admin/single-context-task.md`.
